Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagmahal St. Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF NO. 46 04 June 2008 HON. SANTIAGO R. MARAVILLAS, et al. Sangguniang Panlungsod Members Escalante City, Negros Occidental Dear SP Member Maravillas, et al.' This has reference to your letter seeking the assistance and appropriate action of this Department relative to the attendant circumstances in the failure of that Sanggunian to pass an Appropriations Ordinance for Fiscal Year 2008, said circumstances are hereunder summarized in gist, which you believe are grounds for disciplinary actions provided for under Section 60 of the Local Government Code (RA 7160), viz: 1. The refusal without apparent reason of Hon. Santiago G. Barcelona, Jr., Vice Mayor/Presiding Officer, to cau a special session and to tackle the Annual Budget for CY 2008, despite the certification as ' 'urgent" the passing of an appropriations ordinance of Mayor MeZecio J. Yap, Jr. 2. The walk-out on different occasions by the Vice Mayor/Presiding Officer, by the Temporary Presiding Officer chosen during sessions, and some members of that Sanggunian from the session hau without leave and worse, while session was on-going. 3. The intentional absences of the Vice Mayor/Presiding Officer and some members identified with the Vice Mayor. You are of the proposition that the refusal without reason of the Vice Mayor to call a special session and to tackle the Annual Budget for CY 2008 s. 200±

-2- despite that the said measure was certified "urgent" by the City Mayor is not only a gross neglect and/or dereliction of duty but also an abuse of authority as Vice Mayor and Presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Escalante City; that the intentional absences of some members of the Sanggunian identified with the Vice Mayor are detrimental to the interest of public service and a show of tack of respect to the Sangguniang Panlungsod thereby needing disciplinary action. In the penultimate part of your letter, you requested this Department to issue a ruling for your information and guidance if only to maintain the dignity and respect of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Escalante City. At the outset, may we remind the members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, and that would include the Vice Mayor as Presiding Officer, of one of their mandated duties under Section 458 of the Local Government Code, which provides that: Powers, Duties, Functions and "SEC. 458. Compensation.- (a) The sangguniang pan lungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shaZZ enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shatZ: (i) Approve the annual and supplemental budgets of the city government and appropriate funds for specific programs, projects, services and activities of the city, or for other purposes not contrary to Zaw, in order to promote the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants. " Recognizing the importance of the immediate passage of the Annual Budget of a local government unit, vis-ä-vis the operation of the local government unit concerned and the delivery of basic services for the public welfare, Section 323 of the same Code further mandates the Sanggunian, to wit: Failure to Enact the Annual "SEC. 323. Appropriations.- In case the sanggunian concerned

-3- faits to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian stilt fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shalt be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect untit the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. At this point, it bears to stress that Sections 458 and 323 of the Local Government Code used the word "shall" and thus denoting a mandatory command. Therefore, if the refusal to pass an annual appropriation ordinance denotes a flagrant and culpable unwillingness to perform a duty as mandated by law, those responsible for such delay or refusal will be opening themselves to a possible administrative case of dereliction of duty, neglect of duty or abuse of authority as may be warranted by the evidence, which are grounds for disciplinary action against elective local officials under Section 60 (c) of the Local Government Code. Corollarily, Section 61 of the Local Government Code provides that administrative cases against any elective official of a province, a highly urbanized city, an independent component city or component city shall be filed before the Office of the President. At this point, it bears to emphasize the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in the case of Hagad vs. Gozo- Dadole (251 SCRA 242), where the Supreme Court ruled that the Local Government Code (1991) did not repeal, expressly or impliedly, the Ombudsman Act (1989). Consequently, the jurisdiction of the Office of the Ombudsman to accept administrative complaints against elective local officials is still subsisting and is exercised concurrently with the different jurisdictions mentioned in Section 61 of the Local Government Code. The Supreme Court, however, was quick to caution that the rule on non-forum shopping is applicable, which means that the filing in one jurisdiction will exclude the other jurisdictions. Accordingly, with respect to city elective officials, administrative complaints may be filed against them either before the Office of the

-4- President or before the Office of the Ombudsman. Section 61 of the Code further requires that the administrative complaint must be verified. Considering that your letter is not verified or executed under oath, we regret to inform you that the same cannot yet be treated as a formal complaint against those officials you are complaining against. Thus, you are advised to execute a verified complaint should you opt to file a formal administrative case against them. Importantly, with respect to administrative cases cognizable by the Office of the President, we wish to inform you that the Office of the President issued Administrative Order No. 23 whereby the DILG was constituted as the "Investigating Authority" on administrative cases filed before it pursuant to Section 61 of the Local Government Code. Such being the case, we are thus constrained to refrain from tackling controvertible facts in your letter and render legal opinion thereon as the very issues of facts may be raised before us and might preempt our conduct of formal investigation should, ultimately, you decide to file a formal complaint against them before the Office of the President. In the meantime, it is also our recommendation that you revisit the Internal Rules of Procedure of that Sanggunian and find thereon applicable provisions on internal discipline against erring members. We hope we have enlightened you accordingly. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADER Acting Secreta Legal: 10:43/La cc: U Director Evelyn A. Trompeta DILG Regional Office No. 06 Fort San Pedro, Iloilo City
